name: Performing and Media Arts (BA)
totalCreditsNote: 120 cr per the 2026-27 catalog, at least 100 of them in Arts & Sciences and 80 letter-graded (the app doesn't check those two). Confirm with your advisor.
footnote: Major courses require B- or better. S/U is allowed only when no letter grade option exists; confirm those exceptions with the department. To declare, consult the director of undergraduate studies and complete one departmental course (or transfer equivalent) with B or better, excluding FWS and laboratory classes; it counts toward the major. Cross-listed courses taught by non-PMA faculty count only as the elective and must carry at least 3 credits; instructor eligibility needs advisor review. FWS cannot count toward the major. ENGL 2860 or ENGL 2880 used for the writing requirement cannot count elsewhere. Optional honors requires a PMA GPA of 3.5, overall GPA of 3.0, area-specific prerequisites, and an honors project; performance, film/media production, and design projects also need written analysis. Apply in spring of junior year in consultation with the DUS. The optional Los Angeles spring semester starts in spring 2027: 14 credits including PMA 2401, PMA 3482, PMA 3483, and PMA 3999.

sections.title: Elective Course
sections.note: Production labs do not count. The catalog does not give a separate elective list; PMA courses and cross-listings from its rubric tables are accepted here. Other approved cross-listings and unlisted production labs need department review.

sections.title: Physical Education
sections.note: Two PE classes plus the swim test, a university requirement. PE credits do not count toward the 120.

sections.title: History/Theory/Criticism: Sequence and Breadth
sections.note: Three courses in History/Theory/Criticism, focused on cinema/media studies or performance/theatre studies, plus one course in each other rubric. The 3000-to-4000 pair must form a progression; the third adds depth and breadth. Confirm coherence and PMA faculty instruction with the advisor. Production labs do not count. The catalog does not explicitly say whether the global course may also satisfy a rubric; this checklist uses separate courses.

sections.title: Creative Authorship: Sequence and Breadth
sections.note: Three courses in Creative Authorship, focused on dance composition, directing, or film/media production, plus one course in each other rubric. The 3000-to-4000 pair must form a progression; the third adds depth and breadth. Confirm coherence and PMA faculty instruction with the advisor. Production labs do not count. The catalog does not explicitly say whether the global course may also satisfy a rubric; this checklist uses separate courses.

sections.title: Design: Sequence and Breadth
sections.note: Three courses in Design, focused on costume, lighting, scenery, or sound, plus one course in each other rubric. The 3000-to-4000 pair must form a progression; the third adds depth and breadth. Confirm coherence and PMA faculty instruction with the advisor. Production labs do not count. The catalog does not explicitly say whether the global course may also satisfy a rubric; this checklist uses separate courses. The catalog's Design list has no 4000-level course, so this row takes any 4000-level PMA course other than PMA 4000; confirm it's a Design course with your advisor.

sections.title: Embodied Performance: Sequence and Breadth
sections.note: Three courses in Embodied Performance, focused on acting or dance technique, plus one course in each other rubric. The 3000-to-4000 pair must form a progression; the third adds depth and breadth. Confirm coherence and PMA faculty instruction with the advisor. Production labs do not count. The catalog does not explicitly say whether the global course may also satisfy a rubric; this checklist uses separate courses.

checks.title: First-Year Writing Seminars
checks.missText: needs two FWS courses by the end of sophomore year. A 5 on AP English or a 7 on IB HL English covers one. FWS courses can't count toward anything else.

checks.title: Foreign Language
checks.missText: needs a FLOPI-AS course (a 2000+ course in or about a language), or 11 credits in one language at Cornell (Option 2). Native speakers may be exempt.
